name: Autonomist Marxism
summary: Autonomist Marxism reads capitalism from the working class's side: workers' struggles and refusal of work drive capital's restructuring and crisis, not the reverse. It rejects dependence on party, union or state mediation, extends the working class to the unwaged (housewives, students, the unemployed, migrants), and looks to self-organisation, sabotage and self-valorisation to build communism within present struggles. It condemns Soviet-style socialism as state capitalism and, in its post-operaist strand, argues for a democratic common beyond both private and public property.
scope: Italian operaismo and Autonomia (Tronti, Negri), the English-language current Harry Cleaver named autonomist Marxism, autonomist feminism (Dalla Costa, James, Federici) and Hardt and Negri's post-operaist Commonwealth. It excludes the German Autonomen, autonomist anarchism and insurrectionary groups where they differ, and the separate catalog entry Autonomism covers the movement's wider history.

notes: Hardt and Negri's Commonwealth is read as the post-operaist strand and Tronti's 1965 text as the founding one; where they differ from Cleaver (party, transition) the answer is 0 at low.
